title: Hop-aware replica placement and tail-latency investigation
body:
Summary:

This note captures an ad-hoc investigation into unexpectedly high p95/p99 token latency for multi-GPU LLM inference runs on our v2 cluster. Hypothesis: non-contiguous replica placement across NVSwitch/NVLink boundaries introduces extra hop-count and buffering that interacts poorly with our microbatch/pipeline schedule and NCCL communicator setup, producing intermittent stalls and long tails.

Why this matters:
- We see correct median latency but p99 spikes that break SLOs for low-latency customers.
- The problem appears workload-dependent (longer context lengths and KV-cache heavy workloads show worse tails).
- Fixes that avoid wholesale code changes (placement, env vars, scheduler tweaks) could yield quick wins.

Observed behavior (summary of logs / traces):
- Traces from tracing hooks show spikes aligned with all-reduce steps and KV cache sync points.
- When replicas are placed on GPUs that require an extra NVLink hop (cross-switch or cross-socket PCIe + NVLink), tail latency increases 30–70% depending on sequence length and microbatching.
- NCCL transport shows bursts on socket and uGNI counters (on our interconnect) coincident with increased host staging activity.

Top-level hypotheses (ranked):
1) Hop-count and bisection bandwidth: even though NVSwitch provides high aggregate bandwidth, cross-island transfers funnel through limited links causing queuing and microbursts under simultaneous all-reduce.
2) NCCL algorithm choice + buffer sizing: communicator may be selecting ring vs tree depending on GPU ordering, producing suboptimal packetization for our small, frequent tensors.
3) Host-side copy/doorbell interaction: when a replica is remote enough to require host staging, host CPU / DMA bursts interfere with other processes and create tail spikes.
4) Scheduling alignment: microbatch start times across pipeline stages are synchronized enough to create periodic congestion (epochal pattern) instead of being jittered.

Experiment matrix run so far:
- Microbench 1: nccl-tests all_reduce_perf with 1K, 16K, 64K element sizes across placements (contiguous vs inter-island). Measured bandwidth and latency percentiles.
  - Result: contiguous NVLink placement gave ~25% lower p99 latency for 1K/16K. 64K differences less pronounced.
- Microbench 2: synthetic model workload (B=1 logical microbatch x M=4 pipeline stages) with KV cache enabled, compare placement patterns and collect nsight-system traces.
  - Result: p50 stable but p99 spiky when replicas straddle NVSwitch islands; traces show small stalls at all-reduce start time.
- Env-var trial: toggled NCCL_ALGO (if present), NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVLINK, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 for socket transport isolation, NCCL_DEBUG=INFO to log algorithm selection.
  - Result: forcing P2P to NVLINK reduced p99 in contiguous placements but had no effect when host staging required.
- Staggering starts: introduced randomized microbatch offset (0–1ms jitter) across GPUs to desynchronize microbatches.
  - Result: p99 improved by ~10–20% in several runs; suggests some congestion due to synchronized bursts.

Interesting trace artifacts:
- Short (~200–400us) stalls repeatedly at sequence token index where KV flush/attach occurs. These line up with small all-reduces for cache metadata.
- When cross-island, all-reduce initiation time variance increases (NCCL appears to probe different ring leaders).
- Host CPU saw spikes in memcpy/DMA submission threads in those windows — host staging is implicated.

Measurements and concrete numbers (representative run):
- Workload: 8-way data-parallel replicas, model ~7B, context 2k, microbatch 1, pipeline 4.
- Contiguous placement (all GPUs within same NVSwitch island): p50=18ms, p95=42ms, p99=58ms.
- Cross-island placement (2 GPUs per island across 4 islands): p50=19ms, p95=65ms, p99=98ms.
- With NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVLINK and microbatch staggering: cross-island p99 lowered to ~72ms (not down to contiguous).

Immediate mitigations attempted (what helped vs not):
- Scheduler placement policy: preferring contiguous NVLink island placements reduced tails reliably for high-throughput jobs. (helped)
- Microbatch jittering/desynchronization: small improvement but not a complete fix. (helped a bit)
- Forcing NCCL P2P to NVLINK: only effective in contiguous placements; when host staging unavoidable, negligible effect. (partial)
- Increasing NCCL debug/logging: useful for analysis but adds overhead; be careful on prod. (diagnostic)

Deeper root causes suspected:
- Microburst queueing on inter-island uplinks — multiple transfers align to saturate narrow bisection links intermittently, causing per-token stall and backpressure into the runtime's ring scheduling.
- NCCL algorithm selection depends on effective pair ordering — non-monotonic GPU ids that span islands may cause a fallback to less optimal algorithm for our tensor sizes.
- Host-side DMA scheduling and doorbell semantics create variable latencies when copying large KV cache segments; combined with all-reduce bursts, this propagates into the critical path.

Repro script / commands (sanity):
- nccl-tests: ./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 65536 -f 2 -g 8
- run nsight: nsys profile --output trace --trace=nvtx,cuda,nccl --sample=none --stats=true --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi -- /path/to/inference_binary --replicas=8 --placement=pattern
- collect dmesg & nvidia-smi dmon during run for host/memory spikes.

Recommended next experiments (ranked priority):
1) Systematic placement sweep: run a 16-run sweep across all placement permutations that differ by hop-count (0,1,2 hops) and record p50/p95/p99. Automate placement via scheduler API and log topologies.
2) NCCL algorithm pinning: for each placement, pin NCCL to specific algorithms (ring/tree/tree-radix if available) and measure. Add a tensor-size sweep.
3) Host staging profiling: instrument DMA submission hot paths (perf + flamegraphs) to see if specific threads are contending. Try increasing host-side queue depths or using larger pinned buffers allocated at startup.
4) Adaptive microbatch jitter: implement adaptive jitter that increases when variance is detected and evaluate production feasibility.
5) Small all-reduce coalescing: modify runtime to coalesce adjacent small tensors into fewer larger all-reduces and measure impact.

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- Placement-first policy gives easy wins but reduces scheduler flexibility and packing density. Need to balance latency-sensitive reps vs throughput packing.
- Coalescing reduces number of calls but increases peak buffer sizes and may change memory pressure; must be validated against OOM scenarios.
- NCCL algorithm pinning can be effective but brittle across kernel/driver upgrades. Should be a temporary mitigation.

Action items / tickets:
- RL-1372: placement-sweep automation (owner: Ethan) — implement API to request contiguous island placements and log hw topology metadata.
- RL-1373: allreduce-coalescer spike prototype (owner: Priya) — proof-of-concept in runtime to batch small tensors per step.
- RL-1374: dma-flamegraphs host-side (owner: Zoe) — attach flamegraphs for host staging threads and propose queuing changes.

Notes for on-call / SRE:
- If customers report p99 spikes, quick triage: check replica placement metadata in request trace, look for inter-island placements. If present, attempt reschedule to contiguous hosts (short-term).
- Temporarily enable microbatch jitter flag on the job-level config as a mitigation.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does NCCL choose certain algorithms for our specific ordering and small tensors? Need deeper collaboration with infra or NCCL experts.
- Are there firmware/BIOS-level PCIe settings that materially affect host staging variance?
- Can we opportunistically move KV cache sync points off critical path (lazy sync) without breaking correctness?

Conclusion:
The evidence points to a combinatorial interaction between physical hop-count (NVLink/NVSwitch topology), NCCL communicator behavior, and synchronized microbatch/pipeline schedules that produces intermittent all-reduce-induced tail latency. Short-term: placement policy + microbatch jitter + selective NCCL flags give measurable improvement. Medium-term: coalescing small all-reduces and host DMA optimizations look promising.

Appendix (raw command outputs, brief snippets):
- Example scheduler placement label: "nodeA:gpu[0,1,2,3] island=0; nodeB:gpu[4,5,6,7] island=1"
- Useful env vars to test: NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVLINK, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0, NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, NCCL_ALGO=ring (where supported)

If this is useful we should convert the placement sweep into a small dashboard that correlates hop-count -> p99 automatically.

-- Priya
